preconditions.description: The integer n is within the range [1, 10^5], representing half the number of tree nodes (2n total).
The input contains exactly 2n-1 edges, where edges is the list of (a_i, b_i) pairs parsed from stdin.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= 2 * n and 1 <= b <= 2 * n and a != b for (a, b) in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct nodes in the range [1, 2n].
The input edges form a tree (connected and acyclic) with 2n nodes, where is_tree checks connectivity and acyclicity.

postconditions.description: The output is the number of valid placements of the tree on a 2×n grid, modulo 10^9+7, where count_valid_placements returns the count of distinct placements satisfying the adjacency constraints.

postconditions.expression: count_valid_placements(edges, n) == 0 if any(degree > 2 * n - 1 for degree in get_degrees(edges, 2 * n)) else count_valid_placements(edges, n) >= 0
postconditions.description: If any node has degree > 2n-1 (impossible in a tree), the answer is 0. Otherwise, the answer is a non-negative integer representing valid placements.
